title: The Verdict of the Marlowe Estate
premise: When true-crime podcaster Elodie Iversen exhumes the coffin of Marlowe's founding patriarch and finds it empty, the town's carefully buried history cracks open. Following a trail of forged death certificates, secret heirs, and a decades-old cover-up enforced by the estate's trustees, Elodie discovers the founder may still be alive—and that everyone who helped hide him paid a price in silence. As the trustees close ranks and begin silencing witnesses, Elodie must choose between exposing the truth that will destroy the town he loves and protecting the one person left who knows everything. In the end, Elodie finds the founder alive but broken, broadcasts the confession, and accepts that closing the case costs him his anonymity, his partnership, and nearly his life.
about_author: Vesper Thackeray is a former court stenographer who spent eleven years transcribing small-town trials before turning to fiction. They write from a converted courthouse office in the Pacific Northwest, where they remain stubbornly anonymous.

chapters.title: The Empty Box
chapters.summary: Third-person limited, Elodie. On the centennial of founder Augustus Marlowe's death, Elodie's podcast episode triggers a court-ordered exhumation—only for the coffin to be revealed empty before a crowd and cameras. Elodie's pride in never leaving a case unclosed curdles into dread as the crowd turns on him. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt becomes the weight of consequence.

chapters.title: A Town Built on a Name
chapters.summary: Third-person limited, Elodie. Elodie canvasses Marlowe's founding families and finds a town that worships its dead founder while knowing suspiciously little about his burial. The Marlowe Estate trustees, led by matriarch Constance Hale, offer him a generous grant to 'wrap up the podcast gracefully.' Emotional beat: charm with teeth beneath it.

chapters.title: Six Feet of Nothing
chapters.summary: Third-person limited, Elodie. The coroner's report confirms the coffin was sealed empty in 1924—someone with access and authority arranged the fraud. Elodie's research partner, Juno, digs up a death certificate signed by a doctor who died a week later. Emotional beat: the case stops being historical and starts feeling dangerous.

chapters.title: The Trustee's Smile
chapters.summary: Third-person limited, Constance Hale. Constance convenes the estate's trustees and reveals the empty grave threatens a trust that has quietly governed the town for a century. She orders discreet surveillance on Elodie while insisting to herself it's protection, not menace. Emotional beat: self-deception of the powerful.

chapters.title: Letters from the Attic
chapters.summary: Third-person limited, Elodie. In the estate archive, Elodie finds a bundle of letters in Augustus Marlowe's handwriting dated years after his death. The final letter names a recipient: 'E.I.'—initials that shouldn't exist yet. Emotional beat: vertigo of realizing the case has been waiting for him personally.

chapters.title: What Juno Knows
chapters.summary: Third-person limited, Juno. Juno admits she took the Marlowe assignment for personal reasons: her grandmother was the estate's housemaid and left a sealed diary Juno has never dared open. Their partnership strains as Elodie pushes her to hand it over. Emotional beat: love against duty, in miniature.

chapters.title: The Housemaid's Diary
chapters.summary: Third-person limited, Juno. The diary reveals Augustus didn't die—he fled a scandal that would have ruined the town, and the doctor, the undertaker, and the first trustees conspired to fake his death. Every co-conspirator's descendant still lives in Marlowe. Emotional beat: the past reaching through generations.

chapters.title: Silenced, One by One
chapters.summary: Third-person limited, Elodie. The retired archivist who authenticated the letters is found drowned in his bathtub, ruled accidental. Elodie realizes the trustees aren't protecting a legacy—they're protecting someone still alive. Emotional beat: grief and guilt; the podcast may have killed a man.

chapters.title: Invisible Man
chapters.summary: Third-person limited, Elodie. Flashback chapter to Elodie's last closed case, which destroyed an innocent family and taught him to stay small, stay unseen. His rule—never take a case you can't close—was born here. Emotional beat: the wound that made him.

chapters.title: Constance's Bargain
chapters.summary: Third-person limited, Constance. Constance confronts Elodie privately and offers the truth in exchange for silence: Augustus is alive, ancient and hidden, and exposure will bankrupt the town and the trust that pays its pensions, salaries, and debts. Emotional beat: a corrupt offer that is also, painfully, reasonable.

chapters.title: The Refusal
chapters.summary: Third-person limited, Elodie. Elodie refuses and goes dark, broadcasting from a rented cabin. Juno, torn between him and her family's entanglement in the cover-up, hesitates—and the trustees use her grandmother's diary as leverage against her. Emotional beat: love against duty, the axis tilts.

chapters.title: Trustees of the Lie
chapters.summary: Third-person limited, Constance. Constance's chapter reveals the trust's full architecture: a century of forged documents, bought elections, and quiet disappearances, all maintained by descendants who inherited guilt like property. Her son, Marcus, argues for killing Elodie. Emotional beat: power's corruption passed down like an heirloom.

chapters.title: The Grave Digger's Grandson
chapters.summary: Third-person limited, Elodie. Elodie tracks the undertaker's descendant, old Sam Pike, who confesses that in 1924 he helped carry a living, drugged Augustus out of his own funeral—and that the old man was last seen at a house in the hills that still stands. Emotional beat: the relief of a witness who finally speaks.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Third-person limited, Juno. The archive burns overnight, destroying the letters' provenance. Juno, suspected by both sides, flees to Elodie with the diary and a map her grandmother drew. They reconcile—not with words, but with a shared decision to finish this. Emotional beat: trust rebuilt in the smoke.

chapters.title: The House in the Hills
chapters.summary: Third-person limited, Elodie. Elodie and Juno reach the hidden house and find it inhabited, watched, and wired. Before they can enter, Marcus Hale's men take them. Elodie's recorder, hidden in his coat, keeps running. Emotional beat: terror sharpened by purpose.

chapters.title: Augustus
chapters.summary: Third-person limited, Constance. Constance visits the hidden house and finally meets the man she's spent her life protecting: Augustus Marlowe, 121 years old, lucid, and ashamed. He orders her to let the truth out; she refuses, unable to imagine a town that survives without the lie. Emotional beat: the founder's guilt versus the trustee's necessity.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Third-person limited, Elodie. Held in the estate's cellar, Elodie is offered the same deal as every keeper of the secret: comfort, money, silence. He records his own refusal, understanding that survival here means becoming one of them. Emotional beat: the theme made literal.

chapters.title: Juno's Choice
chapters.summary: Third-person limited, Juno. Juno trades herself for Elodie's release, offering the diary and her silence, and buys him one night of freedom. Her sacrifice forces Elodie to confront that his crusade has made the people he loves pay his debts. Emotional beat: love against duty, resolved by sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Third-person limited, Elodie. Elodie breaks into the town's old radio station—still owned by the trust—and airs the diary, the letters, the recorder tape, and Augustus's own recorded confession, smuggled out by a guilt-ridden Constance. The town listens. Emotional beat: catharsis at full volume.

chapters.title: What the Town Does Now
chapters.summary: Third-person limited, multiple. The town fractures: pensions frozen, statues defaced, families split along the old conspiracy lines. Marcus Hale is arrested for the archivist's murder; Constance surrenders the trust's books. Augustus, exposed, asks to see the town one last time. Emotional beat: truth as both wound and medicine.

chapters.title: The Second Funeral
chapters.summary: Third-person limited, Elodie. Augustus Marlowe dies within the week, and the town buries him in the same grave that once held nothing—this time with witnesses. Elodie and Juno stand apart from the crowd, no longer invisible and no longer welcome. Emotional beat: mourning a man and a myth at once.

chapters.title: The Verdict
chapters.summary: Third-person limited, Elodie. Months later, Elodie releases the final episode: not a verdict on Augustus, but on the living—the town's complicity and his own. He closes the case, keeps the promise to Juno, and accepts that some truths cost more than silence ever did. Emotional beat: hard-won, imperfect peace.
